q: The Leftover Hash Lemma says: if X has min-entropy Hmin(X)≥k and f is a 2-universal hash to {0,1}^ℓ with ℓ ≤ k - 2log(1/ε), then:
opts: f(X) is ε-close to uniform (indistinguishable from ℓ uniform random bits)
f(X) has Shannon entropy exactly ℓ
exp: LHL: hashing a source with high min-entropy using a 2-universal hash function extracts nearly-uniform bits. The output f(X) is ε-close to U_ℓ in total variation. This is the foundation of privacy amplification in quantum key distribution.
